findings.title: Turning `MissingPyprojectToml` into an `anyhow!` string loses the error type that callers may check.
findings.body: `WorkspaceError::MissingPyprojectToml` used to reach callers as a typed error. Now it is replaced by an `anyhow!("{}...", err)` string. Any code above `find_target` that calls `downcast_ref::<WorkspaceError>()` or matches on this case no longer recognizes it. The likely case is the non-strict fallback where plain `uv version` without `--project` or `--preview` prints uv's own version. The test names `version_get_fallback_missing_strict*` point to that fallback, but its code is not in these hunks. If the fallback depends on the type, it now becomes a hard error in normal mode. That would explain why the new `version_get_missing_with_hint` test expects a failure for plain `uv version`. That is a change in behaviour the issue did not ask for; it only wanted a hint added. If the fallback does not depend on the type, the new test contradicts it. Fix: keep the typed error and add the hint where the error is finally reported, for example with `.context(...)` or a hint wrapper that callers can still downcast through. Then check that plain `uv version` behaves as it did before. The same applies to the `--package` branch at lines 341-351.
